findings.title: --flusher-processes defaults to 1, so the per-shard flusher is not enabled by default
findings.body: The PR's stated goal and the SpanFlusher docstring (flusher.py lines 31-32) say the flusher runs one process per redis shard. But the new CLI option defaults to `1`, and SpanFlusher caps process count at `min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards))`. With the default, all shards in the consumer are flushed by one process, so the deployed behavior is essentially unchanged unless the flag is set explicitly. The factory default (`flusher_processes=None` in factory.py line 41, which becomes `len(shards)`) is per-shard, so direct construction and the CLI disagree. Either the CLI default should match the stated design, or the description and docstring should make clear that the flag must be raised to get the new behavior.

findings.title: time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op here, so the flusher-thread wait is a race
findings.body: `test_basic` monkeypatches the global `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None` at line 15. `time.sleep(0.1)` at line 62 therefore returns immediately, and the comment 'Give flusher threads time to process after drift change' is not true. `step.join()` then sets `stopped`, and the flusher thread may exit without running a flush iteration that sees drift=9000. The test then fails at `(msg,) = messages`, or passes only by scheduling luck. The extra `step.poll()` at line 60 also does nothing useful, since SpanFlusher.poll only forwards to next_step. The test should wait on the expected output (for example, poll with a real timeout until messages appear) instead of relying on a sleep that the test itself disabled.

findings.title: join() breaks out of the loop without terminating the remaining flusher processes
findings.body: In the new join loop, once `remaining_time <= 0` the `break` at line 341 exits the loop before the `terminate()` at line 347 for every remaining process. In the old single-process code, the deadline only ended the wait and the process was still terminated. Now, if the deadline is hit during process i, process i is terminated, but processes i+1..n are neither waited on nor terminated. They keep running and can be mid-flush or mid-produce after join() returns. The termination should happen for every process that is still alive, independent of the deadline.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag key: 'shards' here vs 'shard' on the sibling timers
findings.body: The `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` timer uses the tag key `"shards"` (plural), while `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` (line 185) and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` (line 194) use `"shard"`. Dashboards or monitors filtering on `shard` will not see wait_produce data, and it cannot be grouped with the other flusher metrics. The `shard` tag values are also comma-joined shard lists here, while `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` (line 244) emits one integer shard per series, so per-shard breakdowns are not consistent across these metrics.

findings.title: _create_process_for_shard is dead code and nearly duplicates _create_process_for_shards
findings.body: `_create_process_for_shard` (singular) is added but never called. `_ensure_processes_alive` calls `_create_process_for_shards` directly. The two near-identical names make it easy to call the wrong one, and the unused method suggests a restart-by-shard path that does not exist. It should be removed or wired in.

findings.title: New parameter inserted before produce_to_pipe changes the positional signature
findings.body: `flusher_processes` is inserted before `produce_to_pipe`, so any caller that passes `produce_to_pipe` positionally (the 7th argument) now binds it to `flusher_processes`. If a callable reaches `SpanFlusher`, `min(self.max_processes, ...)` in flusher.py raises TypeError when the consumer starts. The new parameter should be added after `produce_to_pipe`, or the call sites should be confirmed to use keyword arguments.

findings.title: New test only checks counts; per-process restart and shard flushing are untested
findings.body: `test_flusher_processes_limit` asserts only the number of processes, `max_processes`, `num_processes`, and that the shard map sums to 4. The new logic that matters most is not exercised: each process flushing exactly its own shards, `_ensure_processes_alive` restarting a single multi-shard process (including the per-process MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS accounting), per-process backpressure in `submit`, and the case where `flusher_processes` exceeds the number of shards. A regression in the shard-to-process mapping or restart path would not be caught.

findings.title: Unrelated documentation change bundled into a span flusher PR
findings.body: The added 'Use hasattr() for unions' anti-pattern has nothing to do with the multiprocessed span flusher. It should be split into its own change so the reviewed PR stays scoped to the flusher and its consumer option.
